content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Spreadsheet Governance and Lifecycle focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Ownership and versioning; Input validation and change controls; Testing and approval; Archiving and retirement. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.code: Input rows → validate types/keys → sort or filter a copy → reconcile row counts and totals
content_blocks.expected_output: Shows a repeatable data-management sequence that keeps the original data available for comparison.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Preserve a raw-data copy, confirm selected columns and sort order, and verify that record counts and unique identifiers still match expectations.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates spreadsheet governance and lifecycle. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

content.task: Build or inspect an Excel example that demonstrates spreadsheet governance and lifecycle; use the example to verify one normal and one edge case, and write down any version or tool dependency.
task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: Shows a repeatable data-management sequence that keeps the original data available for comparison.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
